On Fri, Feb 13, 2026 at 3:30 PM PST marissa.cole@redwood.ai wrote:
> Team — BrightDeal (BrightDeal / acct: 88421) reporting a large p95/p99 spike and reconnects on streaming chat during their US-West peak.

Quick update from runtime: we pulled the traces and logs. Preliminary findings:
- A single routing shard (rs-7f2) hit sporadic GC stalls inside the streaming runtime process due to an edge-case buffer growth when many concurrent short-lived streams join/leave (their campaign opened thousands of short sessions in a 5m burst). GC pause caused token emission delays contributing to p99 spikes.
- KV cache hit-rate dropped for this route because session prefixes vary widely (campaign uses short ephemeral session ids).
- No sign of infra-level network degradation; EC2 host metrics look healthy.

Immediate mitigations we applied (15:50 PST):
1) Throttled new-session acceptance on rs-7f2 for non-authenticated ephemeral routes to reduce buffer churn (should reduce new join spikes).
2) Forced a heap trim and restarted the streaming worker on rs-7f2 (hotfix).
3) Enabled aggressive prefix caching for BrightDeal route and populated several popular prefixes from historical data.

Early post-mitigation numbers: p95 dropped from 830ms -> 180ms, p99 from 2.8s -> ~420ms. Reconnect rate trending down. We'll monitor for the next 2 hours.

— Dev (runtime eng)

Alex — following up on behalf of Redwood leadership. First, thank you for flagging this and for the clear traces; really helpful.

What we did:
- Applied short-term mitigations (throttle + worker recycle + aggressive prefix caching).
- Shifted some of your peak traffic away from rs-7f2 and held capacity at +15% for the campaign window.

Immediate outcomes we observed:
- p95 returned to baseline (~110-160ms) within ~20 minutes of mitigations.
- p99 stabilized under ~500ms for the remainder of the peak window.

Next steps (owner):
1) Runtime (Dev) will run a targeted load-replay with ephemeral-session patterns to reproduce locally and produce a permanent fix (root cause: buffer growth + GC pause under high churn). ETA: 72 hours.
2) CS/AM (Karthik) will coordinate a postmortem call with BrightDeal in 48h and share a mutual action plan for preventing recurrence.
3) Product/SRE will propose a guardrail: automatic protective routing and session-grouping that prevents single-shard GC amplification during sudden short-session bursts. Proposal ETA: 2 weeks.

Commercial: We understand the campaign impact. We're prepared to offer a goodwill credit for the impacted window; Karthik will follow-up with details.

If anything degrades again, please ping the PDINC-3241 incident channel or reply to this thread.

— Evelyn Hart
